ABBA co-founder Björn Ulvaeus has donated more than €100,000 to support Ukraine. The musician directed the funds to the “Keep Ukraine Warm” charitable campaign. He decided to contribute following a dinner with Ukraine’s Ambassador to Sweden, Svitlana Zalishchuk. During their meeting, Zalishchuk explained Ukraine’s urgent need for generators and heating equipment to help protect civilians during the winter. “Ukraine is fighting for us. We know that Putin would like to seize the Baltic region, and that is why I believe we should have supported Ukraine much more from the very beginning,” Ulvaeus told Dagens industri.

🟡 Latest Updates: November 18–19, 2026 🇮🇷 Iran A Sunni Basij member, Behnam Pir Mohammad Shahbakhsh, was martyred in Zahedan after being targeted by armed terrorists. Initial reports indicated that the local Baloch Basij member was attacked by armed terrorists shortly before his martyrdom. Two Iranian border guards were previously reported martyred in Kurdistan. Second Lieutenant Abulfazl Fakham, from the Donis border post of the Baneh Regiment, was martyred while on duty after his vehicle overturned on a difficult road. Conscription soldier Amirmehdi Kianfar, from the Saif border post of the Bastam Border Detachment of the Baneh Regiment, was martyred during an engagement with the PKK terrorist group. A drone was reportedly launched from Omideh Air Base in Khuzestan Province. Iran’s representative to the International Atomic Energy Agency stated that information collected by the agency would inevitably be used to launch further attacks against Iran. Tehran said it had conveyed a clear message during the IAEA Board of Governors meeting, arguing that nuclear facilities cannot be bombed, further attacks threatened, and then precise information and unrestricted access demanded. Iran maintained that information gathered by the agency, although ostensibly intended for safeguards purposes, could be exploited for further military attacks. It called on the Board of Governors to address military attacks against safeguarded nuclear facilities and public threats of further strikes, warning that failure to do so would undermine the credibility of the international nuclear non-proliferation framework. 🇾🇪 Yemen Explosions rocked Saudi Arabia’s Sharurah province following an attack by the Yemeni Armed Forces. Yemeni attacks also targeted Sharurah, while explosions were reported in Riyadh following a drone attack by the Yemeni Armed Forces. Explosions were reported in Abha and southern Saudi Arabia following attacks by the Yemeni Armed Forces. Yemeni ballistic missiles reportedly targeted southern Saudi Arabia, with explosions also reported in Abha and Khamis Mushait. Reports indicated that four Yemeni missiles targeted Saudi positions in the southern region. A Yemeni attack reportedly targeted Najran, Saudi Arabia. Satellite imagery also reportedly showed a large fire at an Aramco oil facility in Riyadh following Yemeni attacks. The Yemeni Armed Forces reportedly targeted an 80-storey building in Riyadh housing Saudi Arabia’s sovereign wealth fund, causing damage to the structure. Saudi aircraft struck a hotel in the coastal city of Mocha, Taiz Governorate, killing and wounding civilians. The strikes reportedly prevented civil defence teams from rescuing victims. Separately, a girl was killed and her mother wounded in a Saudi airstrike targeting homes at the Mawiyah intersection in Al-Ta’iziyah district, Taiz. Workers at a sponge factory in Hodeidah were also killed and wounded. Saudi fighter jets bombed the Sahar district of Saada Province in northern Yemen. E
